summary: Reserved-host throughput ripple: short P99 spikes and sustained p50 drift coinciding with a noisy micro-tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (GraphEdge Analytics, Dedicated) reports recurring throughput instability on reserved-host (cluster rh-us-e-23) across the last 2 business days. Symptoms: transient P99 spikes (2–6s) and a gradual P50 uplift (approx +25% tokens/sec drop) during midday windows. Customer traffic is primarily low-latency chat streams.

Impact:
- User-facing latency spikes for API routes pinned to their reserved-host pool.
- Elevated token billable time for some requests due to retries/fallbacks.
- Customer reports increased tail-latency errors in-app and escalation to CSM.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated (reserved-host rh-us-e-23)
- Region: us-east (primary)
- Model: redwood/gentle-7B-v1 pinned v2026-02-21
- Routes: chat.stream (persistent streaming sockets), chat.sync (short sync requests)

Steps to reproduce (as observed by customer):
1) Run a steady stream of 100 short chat sessions (avg 60 tokens) across 10 concurrent clients for 30 minutes.
2) After ~12–18 minutes, p50 declines and p99 spikes occur for a subset of sessions.
3) Reproduced during customer peak traffic window only.

Observed behavior:
- Allocation logs show short GPU attach delays (100–400ms) plus rare 5xx retry bursts.
- Autoscaler triggers mild scale-ups but then quickly retracts; autoscaler event count shows oscillation.
- Prometheus: increased GPU utilization variance across hosts (one host shows 90–95% with queueing; others 40–60%).
- Kernel metrics show intermittent PCIe stalls on host gpu-23b.

Expected behavior:
- Stable p50/p99 within SLA for pinned capacity with graceful autoscale behavior and no host-level queueing.

Attachments/logs provided by customer:
- API request ids: chat-req-20260305-87a1.., chat-req-20260305-9b02..
- Customer perf dump (link): s3://ge-uploads/2026-03-05/perf-dumps/
- Sample server logs included in attachments.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-05 10:20 UTC: Customer opened support; reported first spike.
- 2026-03-05 12:15 UTC: Support pulled allocator and autoscaler telemetry from rh-us-e-23.
- 2026-03-05 12:45 UTC: Observed a host (gpu-23b) with sustained high RT and elevated PCIe retries.
- 2026-03-06 03:30 UTC: Replayed customer load in staging with synthetic streams; small throughput drift reproduced when a co-located micro-tenant flood was injected.

Hypotheses considered:
1) Noisy micro-tenant on same host causing NVLink/PCIe congestion and kernel stalls.
2) Autoscaler hysteresis: small-scale oscillations cause warmup thrash and prefetched KV cache churn.
3) Scheduler affinity issue leading to uneven GPU packing and long-tail queueing.

Evidence collected:
- Host-level dmesg shows repeated PCIe AER corrected errors around spike windows (timestamps match customer events).
- Topology: gpu-23b shows multiple short-lived CUDA contexts from tenant id t-59f2 (not owned by customer).
- Autoscaler logs show repeated scale decisions within 90s windows (scale-up then scale-down), annotated in PR 1829.
- Prefetch/kvcache metrics show eviction spikes correlating with latency events.

Immediate mitigation actions taken:
- 2026-03-05 13:05 UTC: Support instructed orchestrator to temporarily evict tenant t-59f2 from rh-us-e-23 and rebalance; observed p50 recovery within ~4 minutes on affected routes.
- 2026-03-05 13:12 UTC: Placed targeted host cordon on gpu-23b for further investigation.

Open investigation tasks:
- Capture full PCIe AER logs and escalate to hardware infra for validation.
- Evaluate autoscaler hysteresis thresholds and warmup windows for reserved-hosts vs mixed tenants.
- Audit tenant affinity/scheduler packing heuristics for pinned pools.

Related artifacts:
- Prometheus dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/rh-throughput/rh-us-e-23
- k8s event stream excerpt: https://logs.redwood.local/query?range=1h&host=gpu-23b
comments: 2026-03-05 13:10 - Raj Patel (Support): Noted quick recovery after eviction of t-59f2; suggests noisy neighbor causing PCIe/NVLink contention. Rebalancing reduced p50 by ~30% for observed windows.
2026-03-05 14:02 - Priya Rao (SRE): Collected host dmesg and nvlink counters; attached to PR 1829. Requesting hardware team's input for corrected AER frequency.

2026-03-06 09:20 - Customer (Alvaro, GraphEdge): Thanks — improvement is visible but we still see occasional 4–5s p99 spikes during heavier bursts. Can you advise on long-term fix? We're concerned about tail-latency for SLAs.

2026-03-07 16:45 - Raj Patel (Support): Planned next steps: schedule rolling migration of noisy tenant off reserved-host racks, propose autoscaler cooldown increase for reserved pools, and follow-up with hardware infra for PCIe error root cause.
2026-03-08 11:00 - Hardware Infra (Tara Singh): AER logs collected; initiating hardware swap for gpu-23b due to repeated corrected error rates exceeding threshold.
resolution:
Workaround applied: noisy tenant t-59f2 evicted from cluster rh-us-e-23 and migrated to isolated burst pool; temporary host cordon for gpu-23b. Customer p50 and p99 improved in subsequent windows.

Permanent actions planned:
- Hardware swap of gpu-23b scheduled 2026-03-09 by infra (postponed tests completed).
- Autoscaler tuning: increase cooldown from 30s->120s for reserved-host pools and lengthen warmup window to reduce oscillation (RFC drafted).
- Scheduler change: enforce strict tenant segregation for dedicated pools to prevent mixed-tenancy on reserved-host racks (design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.local/designs/dedicated-isolation).

Follow-up: CSM to update customer on hardware swap and autoscaler rollout timeline. Engineering to track post-deploy metrics for 72 hours and loop back to customer.
